enrichment.short_title: Pinewood bailee liability for lost film stills
key_facts: Arlington acquired Tyburn horror-film negatives and transparencies stored free at Pinewood Studios.
In 2002 Pinewood located most but not all of the claimants' stills and disputes arose over delivery-up terms.
Pinewood accepted it had been bailee of all material but contended missing items had been returned earlier.
The claimants sought damages including verification costs, replacement transparencies, polishing, and lost licence fees.
Burnton J found Pinewood liable for missing material but awarded only £2,545.19 of a much larger damages claim.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Trial of liability and quantum in a claim for delivery up and damages after interlocutory orders for return of stored film material.
enrichment.outcome: Judgment for the claimants for £2,545.19 damages; most heads of loss rejected for lack of proof or legal basis.
enrichment.ratio: A bailee who cannot prove earlier return of goods bears liability for missing items; damages for verification, investigation, and speculative licence losses require proper documentary proof and cannot be established by statements of truth or late disclosed documents.

enrichment.short_title: Territorial scope of unfair dismissal rights abroad

statutes_considered.title: Trade Union and Labour Relations Act 1974

key_facts: Mr Lawson, a British employee of Serco, worked as a security supervisor on Ascension Island.
He claimed constructive unfair dismissal but had not completed the qualifying period unless a health and safety exception applied.
The employment tribunal held it had no jurisdiction because he ordinarily worked outside Great Britain.
The EAT allowed Lawson's appeal using a proximity test based on the employer's presence in England.
The Court of Appeal held ERA unfair dismissal rights apply to employment in Great Britain, not globally.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Employer appeal to the Court of Appeal against an Employment Appeal Tribunal decision restoring jurisdiction over an unfair dismissal claim.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed; the claim was dismissed for lack of jurisdiction.
enrichment.ratio: Section 94 of the Employment Rights Act 1996 confers the right not to be unfairly dismissed in respect of employment in Great Britain; repeal of section 196 did not extend that right to all employees worldwide, and jurisdiction is not determined merely by the employer's residence or by a substantial connection test.

enrichment.ratio: Where capital claims have been finally compromised, periodical payments should generally serve maintenance rather than further capital accumulation; needs alone is not determinative where the payer can afford more, but awards must not subvert capital finality by effectively paying lump sums by instalments.

enrichment.short_title: Partnership mills property and CPR appeal time
key_facts: Aujla sought removal of Sanghera's caution on New Normanton Mills in Derby.
The recorder found a garment partnership and that Sanghera had bought Aujla's share; the mills were held beneficially in equal shares.
Paragraph 3 of the June 2002 order imposed trust obligations relating to third-party lenders not pleaded before the recorder.
Sanghera appealed out of time; the recorder had extended time to file an appellant's notice.
The Court of Appeal set aside paragraph 3, upheld the recorder's jurisdiction to extend time, and ordered transfer into joint names.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal with permission from a county court recorder's order following a multi-day trial on partnership ownership and a caution on registered land.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed in part: paragraph 3 set aside; extension of time upheld; property ordered transferred into joint names subject to Barclays' mortgage.
enrichment.ratio: A lower court may extend time for filing an appellant's notice even after 14 days, but must exercise caution consistent with CPR policy; orders must relate to pleaded issues, and where equal beneficial ownership is found a transfer into joint names should normally follow on dissolution.

enrichment.short_title: GMC erasure appeal for psychiatrist patient misconduct
key_facts: Dr Razak, a Hull psychiatrist, faced GMC charges of improper emotional and sexual conduct towards psychiatric patient Miss A in 2001.
The Professional Conduct Committee found several charges proved, including indecent assault and sexual intercourse, and directed erasure.
Dr Razak appealed on grounds including inconsistent acceptance of Miss A's evidence and a no-case-to-answer submission.
Burnton J reviewed the regulatory standard akin to criminal appeal review and rejected challenges to key findings.
Erasure was held not excessive despite Dr Razak's otherwise good career; GMC costs of £7,868 summarily assessed.

enrichment.outcome: Appeal dismissed on findings and sanction; GMC awarded costs summarily assessed at £7,868.
enrichment.ratio: On a GMC appeal the court asks whether a reasonable committee properly directed could have reached the findings on the evidence; selective rejection of a vulnerable witness's evidence does not necessarily invalidate other proved charges, and erasure may be appropriate for serious sexual misconduct with a psychiatric patient.

enrichment.short_title: Howley Mill Lane bridleway modification challenge

statutes_considered.title: National Parks and Access to the Countryside Act 1949

key_facts: Howley Mill Lane in Morley, Leeds was shown on the definitive map as a footpath about six feet wide.
A modification order redesignated it as a bridleway and altered the stated width to between 1.8 and 3 metres.
The inspector confirmed the order based on 1950s status and 20 years' bridleway user from 1963 to 1983.
The claimant challenged the 'Private Road – Access Only' notice and the historic-evidence route to modification.
The claim failed on prescription grounds; historic re-designation route was legally flawed but not decisive.
enrichment.procedural_posture: High Court application under Schedule 15 paragraph 12 Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 to question validity of a confirmed modification order.
enrichment.outcome: Claim dismissed; 20-year user basis upheld; inspector lawfully modified width particulars; permission to appeal refused.
enrichment.ratio: A landowner notice under Highways Act 1980 section 31 must be erected by the fee simple owner and maintained sufficiently to negative dedication; an inspector's interpretation of notice meaning is reviewable only for legal error or irrationality, and section 53(3)(c) requires newly discovered evidence rather than mere re-examination of old inquiry material.

Whether the notice was erected and maintained by an owner under section 31(7)
Whether historic 1950s evidence satisfied section 53(3)(c) discovery requirement
Power to modify stated path width under section 53 and section 56

enrichment.short_title: Auction misrepresentation damages for protected tenancy
key_facts: Hackney and the MPA auctioned the Chocolate Factory and adjoining Car Park in Shoreditch for £3.925 million to Mr Pankhania.

Tedd QC held the vendors liable under section 2(1) Misrepresentation Act 1967 for deliberate misrepresentation.
Mr Pankhania paid £78,931.25 to secure NCP's departure and incurred delayed development costs.
Damages were assessed at £500,000 using the normal measure of value difference at purchase.

enrichment.outcome: Damages assessed at £500,000 under the normal measure.
enrichment.ratio: Where misrepresentation is treated as fraudulent under Royscott Trust, the normal transaction-date valuation measure applies if it gives a fair result reflecting overriding compensatory principle; the claimant was not locked into the purchase and consequential losses from NCP's tenancy were already embedded in the valuation differential.

Whether retaining the property broke the chain of causation

key_facts: Mr Donovan sought removal of an occupancy condition limiting his Corley nursery dwelling to him and thereafter nursery employees.
